1	/**
     2	 * Repository Detail View — Repo Parallelizer GUI.
     3	 *
     4	 * Renders the Repository Overview page at `#/repositories/:id`, showing a
     5	 * table of every workspace across every project that contains the given
     6	 * repository. Each row displays contextual Project and Workspace columns
     7	 * alongside the shared Branch, Status, and Actions cells.
     8	 *
     9	 * ## Data loading flow
    10	 *
    11	 * 1. `api.repositories.get(id)`  — fetch repository metadata (name, URL).
    12	 * 2. `api.projects.list()`       — fetch all projects.
    13	 * 3. Per project: `api.projects.get(pid)` — filter to those containing repoId.
    14	 * 4. Per matching project: `api.workspaces.list(pid)` — list workspaces.
    15	 * 5. Per workspace: `api.status.get(pid, wid)` — extract the single repo's status.
    16	 * 6. `api.config.webserverUrl.get()` — fetch webserver URL once.
    17	 *
    18	 * Steps 2–5 use `Promise.allSettled` so individual project/workspace fetch
    19	 * failures do not abort the entire load. Failed fetches are silently skipped;
    20	 * when at least one fetch failed but others succeeded a warning toast is shown.
    21	 *
    22	 * ## Router injection
    23	 *
    24	 * Exports `setRouter(router)` so that `app.js` can inject the router for
    25	 * programmatic navigation. The `_router` variable is null-guarded everywhere.
    26	 *
    27	 * ## No polling
    28	 *
    29	 * This view does not auto-poll (refreshing all workspaces across all projects
    30	 * on a timer would be too expensive). A manual "Refresh" button force-fetches
    31	 * all status data and updates rows in-place.
    32	 *
    33	 * @module repository-detail
    34	 */
    35

    37	import { showToast }         from '../components/toast.js';
    38	import { buildRepoStatusCells, updateRepoStatusCells } from '../components/repo-status-cells.js';

    47	
    48	/**
    49	 * Inject the router instance so repository-detail can navigate programmatically.
    50	 * Called from `app.js` before the router starts.
    51	 *
    52	 * @param {import('../router.js').Router} router
    53	 */
    54	export function setRouter(router) {
    55	    _router = router;
    56	}
    57	
    58	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    59	// Constants
    60	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    61	
    62	/** The workspace ID that is always treated as STABLE (no branch switching). */
    63	const STABLE_WS_ID = 'STABLE';
    64	
    65	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    66	// Loading helper
    67	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    68	
    69	/**
    70	 * Render a loading spinner into `el`.
    71	 *
    72	 * @param {HTMLElement} el
    73	 * @param {string} [label]
    74	 */
    75	function showLoading(el, label = 'Loading…') {
    76	    el.innerHTML = '';
    77	    const wrapper = document.createElement('div');
    78	    wrapper.className = 'loading-indicator';
    79	    wrapper.setAttribute('aria-live', 'polite');

    82	    spinner.className = 'spinner';
    83	    spinner.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');

    87	    labelEl.textContent = label;
    88	    wrapper.appendChild(labelEl);

1	# Repository Parallelizer
     2	
     3	Manage multiple related git repositories as a single project — with parallel workspaces, branch orchestration, and a web-based GUI.
     4	
     5	## What Is This?
     6	
     7	When a project spans several git repositories, keeping them in sync is tedious: cloning each one, switching branches across all of them, remembering which repos belong together. **Repository Parallelizer** treats a group of repos as one "project" and lets you create isolated **workspaces** — each with its own branch configuration, cloned copies, and a ready-to-open VS Code `.code-workspace` file.
     8	
     9	Set up a project once, then spin up as many parallel workspaces as you need — one for the main branch, one for a feature, one for a hotfix — without stepping on your own toes.
    10	
    11	## Features
    12	
    13	- **Project-based repo grouping** — register repositories once, then combine them into projects.
    14	- **Parallel workspaces** — create multiple independent workspaces per project, each with its own branch assignments and cloned copies.
    15	- **One-click branch switching** — switch branches across all repos in a workspace in a single operation, with conflict detection.
    16	- **VS Code integration** — auto-generated `.code-workspace` files let you open an entire workspace in VS Code instantly.
    17	- **Web GUI** — a built-in browser UI for managing repositories, projects, workspaces, and branches — no terminal required after setup.
    18	- **Live git status** — automatic polling shows current branches, uncommitted changes, and unfetched commits at a glance.
    19	- **Workspace health checks** — detect and fix configuration drift (missing repos, stale workspace files).
    20	- **Interactive CLI** — a keyboard-driven terminal menu for quick access to setup, server launch, and documentation generation.
    21	- **Private repo support** — per-host credential management for cloning private repositories.
    22	
    23	## How Does This Compare to Git Worktrees?
    24	
    25	Git worktrees let you check out multiple branches of a **single** repository side by side — great when your entire project lives in one repo. Repository Parallelizer solves a different problem: when your project spans **multiple** repositories that need to move together.
    26	
    27	| | Git Worktrees | Repository Parallelizer |
    28	|---|---|---|
    29	| **Scope** | One repository, multiple branches | Multiple repositories, multiple branches |
    30	| **Branch switching** | Per-repo only | Coordinated across all repos at once |
    31	| **VS Code workspace** | Manual setup | Auto-generated `.code-workspace` files |
    32	| **Status overview** | Per-repo (`git status`) | Aggregated across all repos in a workspace |
    33	
    34	If your project is a single repo, worktrees are the simpler choice. If you're juggling a frontend, backend, shared library, and infrastructure repo that all need to be on the same feature branch — that's where this tool comes in.
    35	
    36	## Requirements
    37	
    38	- **Node.js** >= 18
    39	- **npm** >= 9
    40	- **git** >= 2.28
    41	
    42	## Quick Start
    43	
    44	```bash
    45	# Clone and build
    46	git clone https://github.com/Mistralys/repo-parallelizer.git
    47	cd repo-parallelizer
    48	npm install
    49	npm run build
    50	
    51	# Run the setup wizard to create your config
    52	npm link
    53	paralizer setup
    54	
    55	# Launch the GUI
    56	paralizer serve
    57	```
    58	
    59	The setup wizard walks you through creating a `config.json` with your projects folder and storage location. Once complete, open `http://localhost:4200` in your browser to start managing your repositories.
    60	
    61	### Alternative: run without installing globally
    62	
    63	```bash
    64	# Unix / macOS
    65	./menu.sh
    66	
    67	# Windows
    68	menu.cmd
    69	```
    70	
    71	### CLI commands
    72	
    73	| Command | Description |
    74	|---------|-------------|
    75	| `paralizer` | Open the interactive CLI menu |
    76	| `paralizer serve` | Start the GUI server directly |
    77	| `paralizer setup` | Run the setup wizard |
    78	| `paralizer docs` | Generate project documentation |
    79	
    80	## Learn More
    81	
    82	| Resource | Description |
    83	|----------|-------------|
    84	| [Project Manifest](docs/agents/project-manifest/README.md) | Architecture overview and document index |
    85	| [REST API](docs/agents/project-manifest/rest-api.md) | All HTTP endpoints with methods, paths, and response shapes |
    86	| [GUI Frontend](docs/agents/project-manifest/gui-frontend.md) | SPA architecture, routes, and components |
    87	| [Tech Stack](docs/agents/project-manifest/tech-stack.md) | Runtime, dependencies, and architectural patterns |
    88	| [API Surface](docs/agents/project-manifest/api-surface.md) | Exported types, classes, and function signatures |
    89	| [Configuration](docs/agents/project-manifest/constraints.md) | Conventions, validation rules, and config schema |
    90	| [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) | Development setup, build commands, and test instructions |
    91	| [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) | Release history |
    92	
    93	## License
    94	
    95	[ISC](LICENSE)

1	# GUI Frontend
     2	
     3	The frontend is a vanilla JavaScript SPA with no build step, served as static files by the built-in HTTP server from `gui/public/`.
     4	
     5	## Architecture
     6	
     7	- **Routing:** Hash-based client-side router (`#/path`) with named parameter extraction (`:id`, `:wid`).
     8	- **Module system:** Native ES modules loaded by the browser. No bundler.
     9	- **State management:** None — every view fetches fresh data from the REST API on render. Mutations trigger a full view re-render.
    10	- **Styling:** Pico CSS (classless variant) as base layer, with a custom `styles.css` override layer using CSS custom properties. Light/dark theme switching via `data-theme` attribute on `<html>`.
    11	
    12	## Router
    13	
    14	The `Router` class (`gui/public/js/router.js`) manages view lifecycle:
    15	
    16	1. Listens for `hashchange` events.
    17	2. Matches the hash against registered patterns.
    18	3. Calls the previous view's cleanup function (if returned).
    19	4. Clears the `#app` container.
    20	5. Calls the matched view function with `(container, params)`.
    21	6. Stores any cleanup function returned by the view.
    22	
    23	## Routes
    24	
    25	| Hash Pattern | View | Description |
    26	|---|---|---|
    27	| `#/` | `dashboard.js` | Project listing with creation form. |
    28	| `#/repositories` | `repositories.js` | Repository CRUD table. |
    29	| `#/projects/:id` | `project-detail.js` | Project metadata, tabbed repo/workspace/danger-zone management. The workspace table includes a **Health** column: initialized workspaces with health issues show a warning badge with issue count; healthy and uninitialized workspaces show an empty cell. Health is fetched in parallel with status for all initialized workspaces via `Promise.allSettled` (graceful degradation — fetch failures leave the health cell empty). |
    30	| `#/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid` | `workspace-detail.js` | Live git status with countdown-based polling and manual refresh. Health report fetched in parallel on initial load and on every poll/refresh cycle. Unhealthy workspaces render a `.health-alert` card with per-issue rows and fix buttons (`Regenerate File` for `regenerate-workspace-file` issues, `Fix Setup` for `setup-workspace` issues). The header management row includes an **"Open in VS Code"** button (shown only when `workspace.initialized` is `true`; dynamically inserted after a successful Setup without a full re-render). The repository status table has a 4th **"Actions"** column; each repository row contains a **"Browse"** button (shown only when `webserverUrl` is configured, opens `{webserverUrl}/{projectId}/{workspaceId}/{repoId}/` in a new tab via `window.open`) followed by a **"Git GUI"** button that calls `api.workspaces.launch.githubDesktop()`. The webserver URL is fetched once during the initial data load (in parallel with other requests) via `api.config.webserverUrl.get()`. In non-STABLE workspaces, each **Branch** cell is a clickable trigger (`<button class="branch-switch-trigger">`) that opens an inline quick-switch popover via `showBranchQuickSwitch()`. STABLE workspace branch cells remain plain text. |
    31	| `#/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/branch-switch` | `branch-switch.js` | 3-step branch switch wizard. |
    32	| `#/settings` | `settings.js` | Settings view with three sections: **Git Credentials** (add/delete per-host PATs), **Repositories Refresh Delay** (configurable `gitPollingIntervalSeconds`), and **Webserver URL** (base URL of the local webserver; enables the "Browse" button in the workspace-detail view). All non-credentials sections share a single **"Save Settings"** footer button that calls each section's `save()` function in parallel. |
    33	| `#/error-log` | `error-log.js` | Paginated, filterable error log table with expandable detail rows and "Clear All" action. |
    34	
    35	## API Client
    36	
    37	`api.js` exports a namespaced `api` object with six groups:
    38	
    39	- `api.repositories` — `list()`, `get(id)`, `create(data)`, `update(id, data)`, `delete(id)`
    40	- `api.projects` — `list()`, `get(id)`, `create(data)`, `update(id, data)`, `rename(id, newId)`, `delete(id)`, `addRepository(pid, rid)`, `removeRepository(pid, rid)`
    41	- `api.workspaces` — `list(pid)`, `get(pid, wid)`, `create(pid, data)`, `update(pid, wid, data)`, `rename(pid, wid, newId)`, `delete(pid, wid)`, `setup(pid, wid)`, `health(pid, wid)`, `regenerateFile(pid, wid)`, `launch.vscode(pid, wid)`, `launch.githubDesktop(pid, wid, rid)`
    42	- `api.branches` — `list(pid, wid)`, `switch(pid, wid, assignments)`
    43	- `api.status` — `get(pid, wid)`, `refresh(pid, wid)`
    44	- `api.config.credentials` — `list()`, `set(data)`, `delete(host)`
    45	- `api.config.polling` — `get()`, `set(seconds)`
    46	- `api.config.webserverUrl` — `get()`, `set(url)`
    47	- `api.errorLog` — `list(params?)`, `get(id)`, `clear()`, `count()`
    48	
    49	### `api.workspaces` — Health & File Methods
    50	
    51	| Method | HTTP | Description |
    52	|---|---|---|
    53	| `health(pid, wid)` | `GET /api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/health` | Fetch the health report for an initialized workspace. Returns `{ healthy: boolean, issues: Array<{ type: string, severity: string, message: string, fixAction: string, repositoryId?: string }> }`. |
    54	| `regenerateFile(pid, wid)` | `POST /api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/regenerate-workspace-file` | Regenerate the `.code-workspace` file from the current repository list without cloning. Returns `{ success: boolean }`. |
    55	
    56	**`health()` issue `fixAction` values:**
    57	- `regenerate-workspace-file` — missing or stale `.code-workspace` file; surface a `Regenerate File` button.
    58	- `setup-workspace` — uncloned repository; surface a `Fix Setup` button.
    59	
    60	### `api.workspaces.launch` — External-App Launch Methods
    61	
    62	External-application launchers are grouped under the `api.workspaces.launch` sub-namespace. New launcher methods (e.g. "Open in Terminal") should be added here rather than as flat methods on `api.workspaces`.
    63	
    64	| Method | HTTP | Description |
    65	|---|---|---|
    66	| `launch.vscode(pid, wid)` | `POST /api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/launch/vscode` | Open the workspace's `.code-workspace` file in VS Code. No request body. Returns `{ success: boolean }`. 400 if the workspace file does not exist on disk (run setup first). 500 on OS-level spawn failure (logged under Source: `'app-launcher'`, Operation: `'launch-vscode'`). |
    67	| `launch.githubDesktop(pid, wid, rid)` | `POST /api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/launch/github-desktop/:rid` | Open a repository's local clone directory in GitHub Desktop. No request body. Returns `{ success: boolean }`. 400 if the repository directory does not exist on disk (run setup first). 500 on OS-level spawn failure (logged under Source: `'app-launcher'`, Operation: `'launch-github-desktop'`). |
    68	
    69	**Caller contract:** All path parameters (`pid`, `wid`, `rid`) are passed through `encodeURIComponent` inside `api.js`. Callers are responsible for validating that these values are not `undefined`/`null` before invoking these methods — `encodeURIComponent` will coerce them to the strings `'undefined'`/`'null'` rather than throwing.
    70	
    71	### `api.errorLog` Reference
    72	
    73	| Method | HTTP | Description |
    74	|---|---|---|
    75	| `list(params?)` | `GET /api/error-log[?...]` | Fetch error log entries with optional filtering and pagination. |
    76	| `get(id)` | `GET /api/error-log/:id` | Fetch a single entry by numeric ID. |
    77	| `clear()` | `DELETE /api/error-log` | Delete all entries. Resolves with `undefined` on HTTP 204. |
    78	| `count()` | `GET /api/error-log?limit=0` | Fetch only the total count (no entries payload). Useful for badges. |
    79	
    80	**`list()` params shape:**
    81	
    82	```js
    83	api.errorLog.list({
    84	    severity: 'error',   // optional — 'error' | 'warning'
    85	    source:   'clone',   // optional — exact-match on Source field
    86	    limit:    10,        // optional — max entries to return (default 100 server-side)
    87	    offset:   0,         // optional — zero-based page offset
    88	})
    89	```
    90	
    91	All params are optional. Omitting `params` entirely (or passing `undefined`) sends a bare `GET /api/error-log`.
    92	
    93	**`clear()` 204 contract:** The underlying `request()` helper resolves with `undefined` when the server returns HTTP 204 (no body). Callers should not try to read a response value from `clear()`.
    94	
    95	**`count()` pattern:** Sends `GET /api/error-log?limit=0`. The server returns `{ entries: [], total: N }`. Read `response.total` for the count. This is the recommended approach for polling a badge counter without transferring entry data.
    96	
    97	### `api.config.polling` Reference
    98	
    99	| Method | HTTP | Description |
   100	|---|---|---|

   111	| Confirm Dialog | `components/confirm-dialog.js` | `showConfirm(title, message): Promise<void>` | Modal with Cancel/Confirm. Resolves on confirm, rejects on cancel. |
   112	| Form Helpers | `components/form-helpers.js` | `createFormField()`, `validateRequired()`, `WORKSPACE_ID_PATTERN` | Form field generation and validation. |
   113	| Repo Status Cells | `components/repo-status-cells.js` | `buildRepoStatusCells(opts)`, `makeBranchTrigger(branchName, ariaLabel)`, `updateRepoStatusCells(row, repoId, statusInfo, isStable, onBranchCellClick)` | Shared factory for the Branch, Status badge, and Actions `<td>` cells used across repository rows. See [Repo Status Cells Component](#repo-status-cells-component) below. |
   114	| Status Badge | `components/status-badge.js` | `createStatusBadge(gitStatusInfo): HTMLElement` | Git status badge with branch pill and detail chips. |
   115	| Theme Toggle | `components/theme-toggle.js` | `createThemeToggle(): HTMLButtonElement` | Light/dark mode toggle button. Reads/persists theme in `localStorage`. |
   116	| Toast | `components/toast.js` | `showToast(message, type, duration): HTMLElement\|null` | Auto-dismissing notification in `#toast-container`. Message is rendered via `textContent` (not `innerHTML`) — server-controlled strings including git error output are XSS-safe to pass directly. |
   117	
   118	### Repo Status Cells Component
   119	
   120	`components/repo-status-cells.js` encapsulates the reusable Branch, Status badge, and Actions cell-building logic shared between the workspace-detail and repository-detail views. It exports three named functions:
   121	
   122	#### `buildRepoStatusCells(opts)`
   123	
   124	Builds the three shared status `<td>` cells for a single repository row.
   125	
   126	| Option | Type | Required | Description |
   127	|---|---|---|---|
   128	| `repoId` | `string` | Yes | Unique repository identifier. |
   129	| `repoName` | `string` | Yes | Human-readable display name; used in aria-labels. Falls back to `repoId` when no richer name is available. |
   130	| `statusInfo` | `Object\|null` | Yes | `GitStatusInfo` from the API, or `null` when no status data is available yet. |
   131	| `projectId` | `string` | Yes | ID of the parent project. |
   132	| `wid` | `string` | Yes | ID of the parent workspace. |
   133	| `isStable` | `boolean` | No | When `true`, the branch cell renders as plain text (no clickable trigger). |
   134	| `onBranchCellClick` | `function` | No | Callback `(anchorEl, repoId, currentBranch)` wired to the branch trigger button. Only active when `isStable` is falsy. |
   135	| `webserverUrl` | `string\|null` | No | Base URL of the local webserver. When truthy, a "Browse" button is inserted before the "Git GUI" button inside `actionsCell`. |
   136	
   137	**Returns:** `{ branchCell: HTMLTableCellElement, badgeCell: HTMLTableCellElement, actionsCell: HTMLTableCellElement }`
   138	
   139	- `branchCell` carries class `repo-branch-cell`.
   140	- `badgeCell` carries class `repo-badge-cell`; its inner `<div data-repo-id>` wrapper is the polling target.
   141	- `actionsCell` carries class `repo-actions-cell`; contains a "Git GUI" button (always present) and an optional "Browse" button.
   142	
   143	#### `makeBranchTrigger(branchName, ariaLabel)`
   144	
   145	Builds a `<button class="branch-switch-trigger">` styled as inline text. Extracted to avoid duplicating setup in both `buildRepoStatusCells` (initial render) and `updateRepoStatusCells` (polling updates). The click handler is wired by the caller.
   146	
   147	**Returns:** `HTMLButtonElement`
   148	
   149	#### `updateRepoStatusCells(row, repoId, statusInfo, isStable, onBranchCellClick)`
   150	
   151	Updates an existing repository row's Branch and badge cells in-place.
   152	
   153	| Param | Type | Description |
   154	|---|---|---|
   155	| `row` | `HTMLTableRowElement` | The `<tr>` to update. |
   156	| `repoId` | `string` | Repository identifier (used to find the `div[data-repo-id]` badge wrapper). |
   157	| `statusInfo` | `Object\|null` | New `GitStatusInfo` from the API, or `null`. |
   158	| `isStable` | `boolean` | When `true`, the branch cell is rebuilt as plain text. |
   159	| `onBranchCellClick` | `function` | Wired to the branch trigger button in non-STABLE workspaces. |
   160	
   161	Cells are located by CSS class (`.repo-branch-cell`) and badge wrapper attribute (`div[data-repo-id]`) — **not** by hardcoded cell indices — so callers can prepend additional cells without breaking this function.
   162	
   163	> **aria-label fallback:** The branch trigger button aria-label is constructed as `"Switch branch for <name>"` where `<name>` is `row.dataset.repoName` when present on the `<tr>`, falling back to `repoId` when the attribute is absent or empty.
   164	
   165	> **Error handling:** The "Git GUI" button imports `showToast` lazily (dynamic `import('./toast.js')`) inside its click handler to avoid a circular dependency. The button is disabled during the async call and re-enabled in the `finally` block regardless of outcome.
   166	
   167	---
   168	
   169	## Utilities
   170	
   171	| Utility | File | Export | Purpose |
   172	|---|---|---|---|
   173	| Normalise | `utils/normalise.js` | `normaliseRepo()`, `normaliseProject()`, `normaliseWorkspace()` | Maps PascalCase backend keys to camelCase frontend keys. `normaliseWorkspace` now includes `folderPath` (from `FolderPath` in the API response). |
   174	
   175	## Theme Switching
   176	
   177	The GUI supports manual light/dark mode switching:
   178	
   179	- **Mechanism:** The `data-theme` attribute on `<html>` controls the active theme (`"light"` or `"dark"`). Pico CSS v2 reads this attribute for its base styling. The custom `styles.css` remaps all `--color-*` custom properties in a `:root[data-theme="dark"]` block.
   180	- **Toggle:** A `createThemeToggle()` button in the top nav bar (`#theme-toggle-container`) switches between modes on click.
   181	- **Persistence:** The selected theme is stored in `localStorage` under the key `"theme"` and restored on page load.
   182	- **Default:** `"light"` when no stored preference exists.
   183	
   184	## Key Patterns
   185	
   186	### Router Injection (Avoiding Circular Dependencies)
   187	
   188	Views that need `router.navigate()` export a `setRouter(router)` function. `app.js` calls `setRouter()` before `router.start()`. Views never import `router.js` directly.
   189	
   190	Views using router injection: `dashboard.js`, `project-detail.js`, `workspace-detail.js`, `branch-switch.js`.
   191	
   192	### Cleanup Contract
   193	
   194	Views with side-effects (e.g. `setInterval` polling) return a synchronous cleanup function from their entry point. The router calls it before rendering the next view. The cleanup must be returned **before** any async operations, so the router can register it immediately.
   195	
   196	Views returning cleanup: `workspace-detail.js` (clears 1-second countdown interval).
   197	
   198	### Workspace Detail View (`workspace-detail.js`)
   199	
   200	The workspace detail view (`#/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid`) renders live git status for all repositories in a workspace.

    34	```md
    35	# Repository Parallelizer
    36	
    37	Manage multiple related git repositories as a single project — with parallel workspaces, branch orchestration, and a web-based GUI.
    38	
    39	## What Is This?
    40	
    41	When a project spans several git repositories, keeping them in sync is tedious: cloning each one, switching branches across all of them, remembering which repos belong together. **Repository Parallelizer** treats a group of repos as one "project" and lets you create isolated **workspaces** — each with its own branch configuration, cloned copies, and a ready-to-open VS Code `.code-workspace` file.
    42	
    43	Set up a project once, then spin up as many parallel workspaces as you need — one for the main branch, one for a feature, one for a hotfix — without stepping on your own toes.
    44	
    45	## Features
    46	
    47	- **Project-based repo grouping** — register repositories once, then combine them into projects.
    48	- **Parallel workspaces** — create multiple independent workspaces per project, each with its own branch assignments and cloned copies.
    49	- **One-click branch switching** — switch branches across all repos in a workspace in a single operation, with conflict detection.
    50	- **VS Code integration** — auto-generated `.code-workspace` files let you open an entire workspace in VS Code instantly.
    51	- **Web GUI** — a built-in browser UI for managing repositories, projects, workspaces, and branches — no terminal required after setup.
    52	- **Live git status** — automatic polling shows current branches, uncommitted changes, and unfetched commits at a glance.
    53	- **Workspace health checks** — detect and fix configuration drift (missing repos, stale workspace files).
    54	- **Interactive CLI** — a keyboard-driven terminal menu for quick access to setup, server launch, and documentation generation.
    55	- **Private repo support** — per-host credential management for cloning private repositories.
    56	
    57	## How Does This Compare to Git Worktrees?
    58	
    59	Git worktrees let you check out multiple branches of a **single** repository side by side — great when your entire project lives in one repo. Repository Parallelizer solves a different problem: when your project spans **multiple** repositories that need to move together.
    60	
    61	| | Git Worktrees | Repository Parallelizer |
    62	|---|---|---|
    63	| **Scope** | One repository, multiple branches | Multiple repositories, multiple branches |
    64	| **Branch switching** | Per-repo only | Coordinated across all repos at once |
    65	| **VS Code workspace** | Manual setup | Auto-generated `.code-workspace` files |
    66	| **Status overview** | Per-repo (`git status`) | Aggregated across all repos in a workspace |
    67	
    68	If your project is a single repo, worktrees are the simpler choice. If you're juggling a frontend, backend, shared library, and infrastructure repo that all need to be on the same feature branch — that's where this tool comes in.
    69	
    70	## Requirements
    71	
    72	- **Node.js** >= 18
    73	- **npm** >= 9
    74	- **git** >= 2.28
    75	
    76	## Quick Start
    77	
    78	```bash
    79	# Clone and build
    80	git clone https://github.com/Mistralys/repo-parallelizer.git
    81	cd repo-parallelizer
    82	npm install
    83	npm run build
    84	
    85	# Run the setup wizard to create your config
    86	npm link
    87	paralizer setup
    88	
    89	# Launch the GUI
    90	paralizer serve
    91	```
    92	
    93	The setup wizard walks you through creating a `config.json` with your projects folder and storage location. Once complete, open `http://localhost:4200` in your browser to start managing your repositories.
    94	
    95	### Alternative: run without installing globally
    96	
    97	```bash
    98	# Unix / macOS
    99	./menu.sh

201	
   202	**Key behaviours:**
   203	
   204	- **Initial load:** Calls `api.status.refresh()` (force-refresh via live git-fetch) instead of `api.status.get()` (cached), ensuring fresh data even when the polling cache is empty.
   205	- **Refresh toolbar:** A `.workspace-refresh-toolbar` row between the header and the status table displays a countdown label ("Next refresh in Xs") and a "Refresh Now" button. The countdown ticks every second; when it reaches 0, an automatic poll is triggered via `api.status.get()`. The "Refresh Now" button triggers a force-refresh via `api.status.refresh()` and resets the countdown.
   206	- **Countdown-based polling:** Replaces the previous `setInterval(fn, 10000)` approach. A 1-second `setInterval` decrements a counter. At zero it triggers `doPoll()` (cached). A `refreshInProgress` flag prevents race conditions between manual and automatic refreshes.
   207	- **Reactive missing-repos row:** After each poll or manual refresh, the "X repositories have no data" message is re-evaluated. When all repos have status data, the row is removed. When the count changes, the text updates.
   208	- **Setup button in-place update:** After a successful workspace setup, the DOM is mutated in-place: the setup button is removed from `mgmtRow`, an "Open in VS Code" button (`buildOpenVscodeButton`) is inserted before the Rename button, and `workspace.initialized` is set to `true` in the local variable. Only after these DOM mutations does `onSetupSuccess()` fire, triggering an immediate force-refresh and starting the countdown — no router re-render needed.
   209	- **Retry Setup:** The retry button also triggers `doRefresh()` after a successful re-setup instead of reloading the page.
   210	- **Per-repo quick branch switch:** In non-STABLE workspaces, each branch cell in the status table renders a `<button class="branch-switch-trigger">` (styled as inline text with a dotted underline). Clicking it expands an inline popover via `showBranchQuickSwitch()` (dynamically imported from `components/branch-quick-switch.js`), anchored below the clicked cell. The popover shows a filterable list of local branches and a text input pre-filled with the current branch; confirming calls `api.branches.switch()` with a single-entry assignment and triggers `doRefresh()`. STABLE workspace branch cells are plain text with no click behaviour. Both `buildStatusTableSection()` and `updateStatusTable()` receive `isStable` and `onBranchCellClick` parameters so polling updates preserve the clickable style.
   211	- **Repo status cells:** The Branch, Status badge, and Actions `<td>` cells for each repository row are built and updated via `buildRepoStatusCells()` and `updateRepoStatusCells()` from `components/repo-status-cells.js`. These functions locate cells by CSS class (`.repo-branch-cell`, `div[data-repo-id]`) rather than by hardcoded cell indices, so additional cells can be prepended to a row without breaking polling updates.
   212	- **Cleanup contract:** The returned cleanup function clears the 1-second countdown interval.
   213	
   214	### Tabbed Navigation (Project Detail)
   215	
   216	The project detail view organises content into three tabs: **Repositories**, **Workspaces**, and **Danger Zone**. Tabs are implemented with `.tab-nav` / `.tab-btn` / `.tab-panel` CSS classes and ARIA `role="tablist"` / `role="tab"` / `role="tabpanel"` attributes. Switching is handled by a single delegated click listener on the tab nav container. Only one panel is visible at a time (`.tab-panel.active`).
   217	
   218	### Error Log View (`error-log.js`)
   219	
   220	The error log view (`#/error-log`) renders a paginated, filterable table of error log entries fetched from `GET /api/error-log`.
   221	
   222	**Key behaviours:**
   223	
   224	- **Filter bar:** Severity (`all` / `error` / `warning`) and Source dropdowns re-fetch entries on change via `api.errorLog.list()`. Source options are **fetched dynamically** from `GET /api/error-log/sources` (`api.errorLog.sources()`) on view mount and after "Clear All" — no hardcoded list. The filter bar is rebuilt after each sources fetch via `rebuildFilterBar()`.
   225	- **Expandable detail rows:** Each data row (`<tr class="error-log-entry-row">`) is keyboard-accessible (`role="button"`, `tabindex="0"`, `aria-expanded`). Clicking or pressing Enter/Space toggles a hidden `<tr class="error-log-detail-row">` below it containing a `<pre class="error-log-detail-pre">` with the entry's `details` field.
   226	- **Severity badges:** Rendered via `buildSeverityBadge()` using `.severity-badge .severity-error` or `.severity-badge .severity-warning` CSS classes.
   227	- **Timestamps:** Displayed as relative time (e.g. "3 min ago") with the full ISO timestamp in the `title` tooltip. Falls back to the raw string on parse failure.
   228	- **Clear All:** Prompts a `showConfirm()` dialog before calling `api.errorLog.clear()` (HTTP DELETE). Resets filters and reloads on success.
   229	- **XSS safety:** All dynamic text is set via `textContent`, never `innerHTML`.
   230	- **No router injection:** `error-log.js` does not export `setRouter()` — it never needs to navigate away programmatically.
   231	- **No cleanup function:** `renderErrorLog` returns no cleanup — there is no polling or other side-effect to tear down.
   232	- **Shared time utility:** `relativeTime()` is imported from `utils/time.js` (shared with `status-badge.js`'s `formatLastActivity()`).
   233	
   234	**Nav badge:** The `#error-log-badge` span inside the "Error Log" nav link displays a live error count. `nav-badge.js` polls `api.errorLog.count()` every 30 seconds and hides the badge when the count is 0. The error-log view calls `refreshNavBadge()` after "Clear All".
